Linux Reference

The system surface a detection is written against · documented, observed and inferred, kept apart

A technique names a behaviour. A sensor produces a call, a path or a symbol. Something has to hold the map between them, and that is this corpus: a cross-referenced index of the Linux system surface, built to be derived from rather than trained on. It carries no labels and no folds, nothing in it is written by hand, and every record names the method that produced it.

models/datasets/linux-reference

The reference index — and explicitly not a training set: no labels and no folds. It is a cross-referenced map of the Linux system surface, from syscalls and error codes through /proc, library symbols, programs and platform identities, used to derive and validate features rather than fed to a model directly. Nothing in it is edited by hand; it is rebuilt from its sources. It is stratified into three layers with different truth conditions.

COURSE A The spine · documented Upstream and distribution-neutral: the man-pages release joined to the kernel’s own architecture ABI tables. Numbers come from the kernel, not from prose, because man pages carry no per-architecture numbering and guessing it is what produced the previous generation’s errors.
COURSE B Observed · runtime What a real binary on a real system actually did, traced inside a disposable VM harness and keyed by platform. Coverage is bounded to program start-up and destructive or interactive programs are refused by name, so an observed call is proof and an absent one is proof of nothing — a distinction the records carry rather than imply.
COURSE C Inferred · static What a binary declares in its ELF, read without executing it and also keyed by platform. It reaches exactly the programs course B refuses to run, and it is compared against what was loaded rather than merged with it.

No layer overwrites another and every record names the method that produced it. A fact about one userland on one architecture is not a fact about Linux, and what a binary asks for is not what it was seen to do — so the same program on two distributions stays two records instead of collapsing into one that is true of neither.

What it maps

kernel ABI Syscalls joined to their per-architecture numbers, with the calls that are simply not wired on an architecture recorded as absent rather than missing. Error codes carry the inverted index: which calls can return them.
process state The /proc surface as documented, and separately the paths tracing actually touched — which is a larger set, because the documented pages do not index everything a running program reads.
userland Library symbols with the shared object that provides each one; the IPC mechanisms resolved against the spine. This is the bridge that turns an ELF import into a syscall.
programs The section 1 and 8 program surface, with documented flags and sub-commands, and every cross-reference resolved rather than asserted. Where a page states nothing, the record says so and names the layer that will fill it.
platforms Platform identities and what is installed on each, so a fact can be keyed to one userland on one architecture instead of to “Linux”.
network The IANA service, protocol and special-purpose address registries, turned into directional assertions: what an inbound connection to a port means, what an outbound one means, and which addresses should never appear at all.

models/datasets/sources

The inputs: anything a build reads and nothing writes. One directory per origin, named for where it came from rather than for what consumes it, under rules that exist so any figure on this site can be walked back to something with a date and a checksum behind it.

read-only Nothing is edited in place or rewritten by a tool. A correction to a source is a new retrieval, not a patch.
manifested Every directory carries a manifest: what it is, where it came from, the date it was retrieved, the tool that reads it, what it feeds, and a checksum and size per file. A corpus that arrived without one gets a manifest recording what is actually known, including that its origin is unknown.
versioned A versioned source pins its version in the directory name, so a later release is a new directory and a rebuild against either stays reproducible.
unmerged Two origins are two directories even when they describe the same thing, so no record inherits authority it never had.
raw Probe output and scrapes land unparsed. Parsing belongs to the tools, and its result belongs to a generated dataset — never back in the source.
no telemetry Collection runs live elsewhere: they evaluate the model rather than feed it, and that separation is the leakage boundary.

Between them these two directories are what makes a coverage claim traceable. An event key on this site resolves to an analytic and a data component, that resolves to what the kernel actually exposes, and that resolves in turn to a documented page, a traced run or an ELF header — each with a retrieval date and a hash standing behind it.
